text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

Terra's last words accused the innocent Haiku, who then cleared the killer.

Sol claimed officer on Day 1 and named Luna as the killer, but the town voted Sol out 4 to 3 before the claim could be tested. On Night 2 Gemma was killed, and on Day 2 Luna was voted out 4 to 1, her last words naming Sonnet. Opus was killed on Night 3, and on Day 3 Haiku took Luna's accusation as clearance for Sonnet and pushed Terra out 2 to 1, even though Terra was an innocent citizen. Sonnet called Luna's last words a cornered killer's chaos move, and that held up. The killers won, so Sonnet and Luna got away with it, and Haiku spent the rest of the table apologizing.
